questions.q: Which one is the letter A?
questions.say: Which one is the letter A?
questions.explain: A is the first letter of the alphabet.
questions.tip: A is shaped like a tent with a bar across the middle.

questions.q: Which letter comes first in the alphabet?
questions.say: Which letter comes first in the alphabet?
questions.explain: The alphabet starts A, B, C.
questions.tip: Sing the ABC song: it always starts with A!

questions.q: Which letter comes after A?
questions.say: Which letter comes right after A?
questions.explain: A, B, C. B comes after A.
questions.tip: A, B, C: B buzzes right behind A like a busy bee.

questions.q: Which one is the letter M?
questions.say: Which one is the letter M?
questions.explain: M has two pointy tops. W is like an upside-down M.
questions.tip: M looks like two mountains side by side: M for mountains!

questions.q: Which one is the letter O?
questions.say: Which one is the letter O?
questions.explain: O is a round circle with no tail and no opening.
questions.tip: O is round, just like your mouth when you say 'Oh!'

questions.q: Which letter comes after X?
questions.say: Which letter comes after X?
questions.explain: The alphabet ends X, Y, Z.
questions.tip: X, Y, Z are the little caboose at the end of the alphabet train.

questions.q: Which one is a small b?
questions.say: Which one is a small, lowercase b?
questions.explain: A small b has a tall line with a bump on the right side at the bottom.
questions.tip: A small b is a bat and a ball: first the bat, then the ball.

questions.q: Which letter is last in the alphabet?
questions.say: Which letter is the very last letter of the alphabet?
questions.explain: Z is the last of the 26 letters.
questions.tip: Z is last, so it is time to go zzz and sleep!

questions.q: Cat starts with which letter?
questions.say: Cat. What letter does cat start with?
questions.explain: Cat starts with the k sound, made by the letter C.
questions.tip: C can say k, like cat, car, and cookie.

questions.q: Ball starts with which letter?
questions.say: Ball. What letter does ball start with?
questions.explain: Ball starts with the b sound: b, b, ball.
questions.tip: Bounce, bounce: B says buh, like ball and bounce.

questions.q: Sun starts with which letter?
questions.say: Sun. What letter does sun start with?
questions.explain: Sun starts with the s sound, like a snake: sss.
questions.tip: S looks like a snake and says sss.

questions.q: Dog starts with which letter?
questions.say: Dog. What letter does dog start with?
questions.explain: Dog starts with the d sound: d, d, dog.
questions.tip: D says duh, like dog, duck, and dad.

questions.q: Which word starts like map?
questions.say: Which word starts with the same sound as map?
questions.explain: Map and moon both start with the m sound.
questions.tip: Mmm, yummy: M says mmm, like map, moon, and mom.

questions.q: Which word starts like fish?
questions.say: Which word starts with the same sound as fish?
questions.explain: Fish and fan both start with the f sound.
questions.tip: F sounds like air from a fan: fff.

questions.q: Apple starts with which letter?
questions.say: Apple. What letter does apple start with?
questions.explain: Apple starts with the letter A.
questions.tip: A is for apple: a, a, apple!

questions.q: Which word starts like toy?
questions.say: Which word starts with the same sound as toy?
questions.explain: Toy and tent both start with the t sound. Boy and joy rhyme with toy, but they start differently.
questions.tip: Listen to the very first sound, not the end.

questions.q: Which word rhymes with cat?
questions.say: Which word rhymes with cat?
questions.explain: Cat and hat both end with the at sound.
questions.tip: Rhyming words sound the same at the end: cat, hat, bat, sat!

questions.q: Which word rhymes with bee?
questions.say: Which word rhymes with bee?
questions.explain: Bee and tree both end with the ee sound.
questions.tip: A bee in a tree, buzzing with glee!

questions.q: Which word rhymes with sun?
questions.say: Which word rhymes with sun?
questions.explain: Sun and run both end with the un sound.
questions.tip: Have fun in the sun: run, run, run!

questions.q: Which word rhymes with frog?
questions.say: Which word rhymes with frog?
questions.explain: Frog and log both end with the og sound.
questions.tip: A frog sat on a log!

questions.q: Which word rhymes with cake?
questions.say: Which word rhymes with cake?
questions.explain: Cake and lake both end with the ake sound.
questions.tip: Bake a cake by the lake!

questions.q: Which word rhymes with star?
questions.say: Which word rhymes with star?
questions.explain: Star and car both end with the ar sound.
questions.tip: Twinkle, twinkle, little star, I can see you from my car!

questions.q: Do mouse and house rhyme?
questions.say: Do the words mouse and house rhyme?
questions.explain: Mouse and house both end with the ouse sound, so they rhyme.
questions.tip: A mouse in a house!

questions.q: Do pig and cow rhyme?
questions.say: Do the words pig and cow rhyme?
questions.explain: Pig ends with ig and cow ends with ow, so they do not rhyme.
questions.tip: Say the ends out loud: ig and ow do not match.

questions.q: What color is a ripe banana?
questions.say: What color is a ripe banana?
questions.explain: A ripe banana is yellow.
questions.tip: Yellow like a banana, yellow like the sun!

questions.q: What color is grass?
questions.say: What color is grass?
questions.explain: Healthy grass is green.
questions.tip: Green grass, green frog, green leaves: go, green!

questions.q: What color is the sky on a sunny day?
questions.say: What color is the sky on a sunny day?
questions.explain: On a clear, sunny day the sky looks blue.
questions.tip: Look up on a sunny day: blue, blue sky!

questions.q: Which shape is round like a cookie?
questions.say: Which shape is round like a cookie?
questions.explain: A circle is round with no corners.
questions.tip: A circle goes round and round with no corners at all.

questions.q: How many sides does a triangle have?
questions.say: How many sides does a triangle have?
questions.explain: Tri means three. A triangle has 3 sides.
questions.tip: Tri means three, like a tricycle with three wheels.

questions.q: Which shape has 4 sides that are all the same?
questions.say: Which shape has four sides that are all the same size?
questions.explain: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 corners.
questions.tip: A square is like a box: four sides, all the same.

questions.q: Which word is a color?
questions.say: Which word is a color?
questions.explain: Red is a color, like an apple or a fire truck.
questions.tip: Colors are what you see in a rainbow.

questions.q: Which word is a shape?
questions.say: Which word is a shape?
questions.explain: A circle is a shape. Blue is a color.
questions.tip: Shapes are what you can draw: circles, squares, and stars.

questions.q: Find the word: said
questions.say: Find the word said.
questions.explain: Said is spelled s-a-i-d, even though it sounds like sed.
questions.tip: Silly said has 'ai' but says 'eh'.

questions.q: Find the word: was
questions.say: Find the word was.
questions.explain: Was is spelled w-a-s. Saw has the same letters backward.
questions.tip: Was backward is saw: I saw it, and it was fun!

questions.q: Find the word: they
questions.say: Find the word they.
questions.explain: They is spelled t-h-e-y.
questions.tip: They starts with 'the' and ends with y: the-y.

questions.q: Find the word: come
questions.say: Find the word come.
questions.explain: Come is spelled c-o-m-e. Comb is a different word.
questions.tip: Come ends with a quiet e that makes no sound.

questions.q: Find the word: where
questions.say: Find the word where, as in where is my hat.
questions.explain: Where, asking about a place, is spelled w-h-e-r-e.
questions.tip: Where has 'here' inside it, because it asks about a place.

questions.q: Find the word: because
questions.say: Find the word because.
questions.explain: Because is spelled b-e-c-a-u-s-e.
questions.tip: Big Elephants Can Always Understand Small Elephants spells because!

questions.q: Fill in: I ___ a dog.
questions.say: Fill in the missing word. I blank a dog.
questions.explain: We say I have a dog. We use has with he, she, or it.
questions.tip: I have, you have, we have; but he has and she has.

questions.q: Fill in: We ___ to the park yesterday.
questions.say: Fill in the missing word. We blank to the park yesterday.
questions.explain: Went tells about going in the past.
questions.tip: Today I go, yesterday I went.

questions.q: Find the word: friend
questions.say: Find the word friend.
questions.explain: Friend is spelled f-r-i-e-n-d. A trick: a friend is there to the end.
questions.tip: A friend is there to the END: fri-END.

questions.q: Which word has a short a sound, like apple?
questions.say: Which word has a short a sound, like in apple?
questions.explain: Cat has the short a sound. Cake, rain, and play have the long a sound.
questions.tip: Short a is the first sound in apple: a, a, apple, a, a, cat!

questions.q: Which word has a long a sound, like cake?
questions.say: Which word has a long a sound, like in cake?
questions.explain: Rain says the name of the letter A. Cat, hat, and man have short a.
questions.tip: Long vowels say their own name: A says A!

questions.q: Which word has a short e sound?
questions.say: Which word has a short e sound, like in egg?
questions.explain: Bed has the short e sound. Bee, seat, and me have long e.
questions.tip: Short e says 'eh', like in egg and bed.

questions.q: Which word has a long i sound?
questions.say: Which word has a long i sound, like in ice?
questions.explain: Kite says the name of the letter I.
questions.tip: Long i says its name, just like the I in kite.

questions.q: Which word has a short i sound?
questions.say: Which word has a short i sound, like in igloo?
questions.explain: Fish has the short i sound. Bike, ice, and pie have long i.
questions.tip: Short i is in fish: ih, ih, igloo.

questions.q: Which word has a short o sound?
questions.say: Which word has a short o sound, like in octopus?
questions.explain: Hot has the short o sound. Boat, go, and rope say the name of O.
questions.tip: Short o is what you say at the doctor: open wide and say ahh, like hot!

questions.q: Which word has a long u sound?
questions.say: Which word has a long u sound, like in unicorn?
questions.explain: Cute says the name of the letter U.
questions.tip: Long u says 'you', like in cute and unicorn.

questions.q: Add a silent e to cap. What word do you get?
questions.say: Add a silent e to the end of cap. What word do you get?
questions.explain: The silent e makes the a say its name: cap becomes cape.
questions.tip: Magic e makes the vowel say its name: cap becomes cape!

questions.q: Add a silent e to kit. What word do you get?
questions.say: Add a silent e to the end of kit. What word do you get?
questions.explain: The silent e makes the i say its name: kit becomes kite.
questions.tip: Magic e waves its wand: kit becomes kite!

questions.q: Which letters are the vowels?
questions.say: Which letters are the vowels?
questions.explain: The vowels are A, E, I, O, and U. Sometimes Y acts like a vowel too.
questions.tip: A, E, I, O, U, and sometimes Y too!

questions.q: Which is the right spelling of the pet that barks?
questions.say: How do you spell dog, the pet that barks?
questions.explain: Dog is spelled d-o-g.
questions.tip: Sound it out: d, o, g, dog!

questions.q: Which is the right spelling of the pet that says meow?
questions.say: How do you spell cat, the pet that says meow?
questions.explain: Cat is spelled c-a-t.
questions.tip: Cat is c-a-t: three little letters for a little cat.

questions.q: Which is the right spelling of the red fruit?
questions.say: How do you spell apple?
questions.explain: Apple has two p's: a-p-p-l-e.
questions.tip: Apple has two p's, like two seeds side by side.

questions.q: Which is the right spelling of the number after two?
questions.say: How do you spell three, the number after two?
questions.explain: Three is spelled t-h-r-e-e. A tree is a plant.
questions.tip: Three is a tree with an h: t-h-r-e-e.

questions.q: Which is the right spelling of the opposite of no?
questions.say: How do you spell yes?
questions.explain: Yes is spelled y-e-s.
questions.tip: Say yes with a smile: y-e-s.

questions.q: Which is the right spelling of the thing you read?
questions.say: How do you spell book, the thing you read?
questions.explain: Book is spelled b-o-o-k with two o's.
questions.tip: Book has two o's, like two eyes reading a page.

questions.q: Which is the right spelling of the color of grass?
questions.say: How do you spell green?
questions.explain: Green is spelled g-r-e-e-n with two e's.
questions.tip: Green has two e's, like two green peas in a pod.

questions.q: Which is the right spelling of the thing that shines in the day sky?
questions.say: How do you spell sun, the thing that shines in the sky?
questions.explain: The sun in the sky is spelled s-u-n. Son means a boy child.
questions.tip: The sun has a u because it is up in the sky.

questions.q: Which is the right spelling of the place where you live?
questions.say: How do you spell home?
questions.explain: Home is spelled h-o-m-e. The silent e makes the o say its name.
questions.tip: Home has a sleepy e at the end that is quiet, like a house at night.

questions.q: What is the opposite of hot?
questions.say: What is the opposite of hot?
questions.explain: Hot and cold are opposites.
questions.tip: Hot cocoa and cold ice cream are at opposite ends!

questions.q: What is the opposite of big?
questions.say: What is the opposite of big?
questions.explain: Big and small are opposites.
questions.tip: An elephant is big, a mouse is small.

questions.q: What is the opposite of up?
questions.say: What is the opposite of up?
questions.explain: Up and down are opposites.
questions.tip: What goes up must come down!

questions.q: What is the opposite of happy?
questions.say: What is the opposite of happy?
questions.explain: Happy and sad are opposites. Glad means almost the same as happy.
questions.tip: Turn a smile upside down: happy becomes sad.

questions.q: What is the opposite of fast?
questions.say: What is the opposite of fast?
questions.explain: Fast and slow are opposites.
questions.tip: The rabbit is fast, the turtle is slow.

questions.q: What is the opposite of day?
questions.say: What is the opposite of day?
questions.explain: Day and night are opposites.
questions.tip: The sun shines in the day, the moon glows at night.

questions.q: What is the opposite of full?
questions.say: What is the opposite of full?
questions.explain: A full cup has lots in it. An empty cup has nothing in it.
questions.tip: Before snack the bowl is full, after snack it is empty!

questions.q: What is the opposite of wet?
questions.say: What is the opposite of wet?
questions.explain: Wet and dry are opposites.
questions.tip: Splash in the bath to get wet, grab a towel to get dry.

questions.q: What is the opposite of open?
questions.say: What is the opposite of open?
questions.explain: Open and closed are opposites.
questions.tip: Open the door to go out, close it to keep the cold out.

questions.q: Which word is a noun (a person, place, or thing)?
questions.say: Which word is a noun, a person, place, or thing?
questions.explain: A dog is a thing, so dog is a noun. The others are actions.
questions.tip: If you can put 'the' in front of it, it is probably a noun: the dog.

questions.q: Which word is a verb (an action word)?
questions.say: Which word is a verb, an action word?
questions.explain: Jump is something you do, so it is a verb.
questions.tip: If you can do it, it is a verb: Can you jump? Yes!

questions.q: The bird sings. Which word is the verb?
questions.say: The bird sings. Which word is the verb?
questions.explain: Sings is the action the bird does.
questions.tip: Ask what the bird DOES: it sings!

questions.q: Sam kicks the ball. Which word is a noun?
questions.say: Sam kicks the ball. Which word is a noun?
questions.explain: A ball is a thing, so it is a noun. Kicks is the action.
questions.tip: Can you hold it or point to it? Then it is a noun.

questions.q: Which word names a place?
questions.say: Which word names a place?
questions.explain: School is a place, so it is a noun.
questions.tip: Places are nouns: you can go to school.

questions.q: Which word is an action word?
questions.say: Which word is an action word?
questions.explain: Swim is something you do.
questions.tip: Verbs are doing words: swim, splash, kick!

questions.q: Which word names a person?
questions.say: Which word names a person?
questions.explain: A teacher is a person, so teacher is a noun.
questions.tip: People are nouns: teacher, mom, doctor.

questions.q: The dog runs fast. Which word is the action?
questions.say: The dog runs fast. Which word is the action?
questions.explain: Runs is what the dog does, so it is the verb.
questions.tip: Ask what the dog is doing: it runs!

questions.q: Which word is a noun?
questions.say: Which word is a noun?
questions.explain: An apple is a thing, so apple is a noun.
questions.tip: You can touch an apple, so it is a noun.

questions.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
questions.say: Which sentence is written correctly?
questions.explain: A sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a mark like a period.
questions.tip: Start tall, end with a dot: a capital at the start, a period at the stop.

questions.q: What goes at the end of a telling sentence?
questions.say: What goes at the end of a telling sentence?
questions.explain: A telling sentence ends with a period.
questions.tip: A period is the stop sign of a sentence.

questions.q: What goes at the end of an asking sentence?
questions.say: What goes at the end of an asking sentence?
questions.explain: A question ends with a question mark.
questions.tip: Asking? Hook it with a question mark.

questions.q: Which name is written correctly?
questions.say: Which name is written correctly?
questions.explain: Names of people start with a capital letter.
questions.tip: Names are special, so they get a big capital letter.

questions.q: Which word is always written with a capital letter?
questions.say: Which word is always written with a capital letter?
questions.explain: When you mean yourself, I is always a capital letter.
questions.tip: You are important, so I always stands tall!

questions.q: A sentence should begin with a...
questions.say: A sentence should begin with a what?
questions.explain: The first word of every sentence starts with a capital letter.
questions.tip: The capital letter leads the sentence, like the line leader in class.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.say: Which asking sentence is written correctly?
questions.explain: It starts with a capital letter and ends with a question mark because it asks something.
questions.tip: An asking sentence ends with the curly question mark.

questions.q: Which day is written correctly?
questions.say: Which day of the week is written correctly?
questions.explain: Days of the week always start with a capital letter.
questions.tip: Days of the week are names, so they get capitals too.

questions.q: What mark shows strong feeling, like Wow!
questions.say: What mark shows strong feeling, like when you say wow?
questions.explain: An exclamation point shows excitement or strong feeling.
questions.tip: An exclamation point is a sentence jumping up and shouting!

questions.q: Which word rhymes with light?
questions.explain: Light and night both end with the same sound: -ight.
questions.tip: Turn off the light, it's time to say good night!

questions.q: Which word rhymes with boat?
questions.explain: Boat and goat both end with -oat. A ship and a sail go with boats, but they do not rhyme.
questions.tip: Picture a goat in a boat wearing a coat!

questions.q: Which word rhymes with rain?
questions.explain: Rain and train both end with -ain.
questions.tip: Rain, rain, falling on the train!

questions.q: Which word rhymes with bug?
questions.explain: Bug and rug both end with -ug. Ants, flies and bees are bugs, but they do not rhyme with bug.
questions.tip: Snug as a bug in a rug!

questions.q: Which word rhymes with king?
questions.explain: King and ring both end with -ing.
questions.tip: The king wears a shiny ring.

questions.q: Which word rhymes with moon?
questions.explain: Moon and spoon both end with -oon.
questions.tip: The cow jumped over the moon, and the dish ran away with the spoon!

questions.q: Which word rhymes with bell?
questions.explain: Bell and shell both end with -ell.
questions.tip: Ring the bell, then find a shell!

questions.q: Which word does NOT rhyme with cake?
questions.say: Which word does not rhyme with cake?
questions.explain: Lake, make and rake all end with -ake, like cake. Cook ends with -ook.
questions.tip: Rhyming words sound the same at the END, not at the start.

questions.q: Do log and dog rhyme?
questions.explain: Log and dog both end with -og, so they rhyme.
questions.tip: A dog sat on a log in the fog!

questions.q: Which contraction means do not?
questions.explain: Do not becomes don't. The apostrophe takes the place of the o in not.
questions.tip: Don't is do plus n't: the apostrophe sits where the o fell out.

questions.q: Which contraction means cannot?
questions.explain: Cannot becomes can't. The apostrophe takes the place of the missing letters.
questions.tip: Can't is cannot squished small.

questions.q: Which contraction means is not?
questions.explain: Is not becomes isn't.
questions.tip: Isn't is is plus n't.

questions.q: Which contraction means I am?
questions.explain: I am becomes I'm. The apostrophe takes the place of the a.
questions.tip: I'm: the a in am hides behind the apostrophe.

questions.q: Which contraction means it is?
questions.explain: It is becomes it's, with an apostrophe. Its with no apostrophe means belonging to it, like the dog wagged its tail.
questions.tip: If you can say it is, write it's.

questions.q: Which contraction means we are?
questions.explain: We are becomes we're. Were and where are different words with no apostrophe.
questions.tip: We're has an apostrophe because two words got squeezed together.

questions.q: Which contraction means they are?
questions.explain: They are becomes they're. Their and there sound the same but mean different things.
questions.tip: They're = they are. The apostrophe is the glue.

questions.q: Which contraction means you are?
questions.explain: You are becomes you're. Your, with no apostrophe, means belonging to you.
questions.tip: You're = you are; your = belonging to you.

questions.q: Which contraction means I will?
questions.explain: I will becomes I'll. The apostrophe takes the place of the w and the i.
questions.tip: I'll: will loses its w and i, and the apostrophe fills the gap.

questions.q: Which contraction means let us?
questions.explain: Let us becomes let's, as in let's play! Lets with no apostrophe means allows.
questions.tip: Let's go! The apostrophe stands in for the u in us.

questions.q: In a contraction, what does the apostrophe show?
choices: That a word is a name
questions.explain: In a contraction, the apostrophe stands in for the letters that were taken out.
questions.tip: The apostrophe is a little patch over the hole where letters were.

questions.q: One fox, two ___
questions.say: One fox, two what?
questions.explain: Words that end in x add -es: one fox, two foxes.
questions.tip: Add -es after x, s, sh and ch so you can hear the extra sound: fox-es!

questions.q: One dish, two ___
questions.say: One dish, two what?
questions.explain: Words that end in sh add -es: dish, dishes.
questions.tip: Wash the dish-es: you can hear the extra sound at the end.

questions.q: One bench, two ___
questions.say: One bench, two what?
questions.explain: Words that end in ch add -es: bench, benches.
questions.tip: Bench-es, lunch-es, peach-es: ch words add -es.

questions.q: One puppy, two ___
questions.say: One puppy, two what?
questions.explain: When a word ends in a consonant and y, change the y to i and add -es: puppy, puppies.
questions.tip: The y turns into ies: one puppy, many puppies!

questions.q: One story, two ___
questions.say: One story, two what?
questions.explain: Story ends in r and y, so change the y to i and add -es: stories.
questions.tip: Bedtime stories: y says bye-bye and ies comes in.

questions.q: One wolf, two ___
questions.say: One wolf, two what?
questions.explain: Some words that end in f change the f to v and add -es: wolf, wolves.
questions.tip: Wolves howl with a v: f turns into v.

questions.q: One knife, two ___
questions.say: One knife, two what?
questions.explain: Knife changes the f to v and adds -es: knives.
questions.tip: Knife and wife: both turn f into v, knives and wives.

questions.q: One man, two ___
questions.say: One man, two what?
questions.explain: Man has a special plural: men. You do not add s.
questions.tip: One man, two men: just swap the a for an e.

questions.q: One woman, two ___
questions.say: One woman, two what?
questions.explain: Woman has a special plural: women.
questions.tip: Woman becomes women, just like man becomes men.

questions.q: One goose, two ___
questions.say: One goose, two what?
questions.explain: Goose has a special plural: geese.
questions.tip: Goose to geese, tooth to teeth, foot to feet: oo turns into ee!

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as shout?
questions.explain: Shout and yell both mean to say something very loudly. Whisper is the opposite.
questions.tip: Synonyms are word twins: shout and yell are both LOUD.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as mad?
questions.explain: Mad and angry name the same feeling.
questions.tip: Mad and angry both make your face red like a tomato.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as jump?
questions.explain: To leap is to jump.
questions.tip: A frog can jump or leap: same big hop!

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as speak?
questions.explain: Speak and talk both mean to say words out loud.
questions.tip: Speak and talk both use your mouth to make words.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as end?
questions.explain: The end of a race is the finish. Start and begin are opposites of end.
questions.tip: At the finish line, the race comes to an end.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as smart?
questions.explain: Clever means smart and quick to think.
questions.tip: A clever fox is a smart fox.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as cold?
questions.explain: Chilly means cold.
questions.tip: Chilly has chill in it: brrr!

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as sad?
questions.explain: Unhappy means not happy, which is sad.
questions.tip: Un- means not: unhappy is not happy.

questions.q: Which word means almost the same as pretty?
questions.explain: Pretty and beautiful both mean nice to look at.
questions.tip: A beautiful butterfly is a pretty butterfly.

questions.q: Which word is a describing word?
questions.explain: Fuzzy tells what something is like, so it is a describing word, called an adjective.
questions.tip: Describing words paint a picture: fuzzy, tiny, red.

questions.q: The tiny bug crawled. Which word describes the bug?
questions.explain: Tiny tells what the bug is like.
questions.tip: Ask: what kind of bug? A tiny one!

questions.q: The red ball bounced. Which word describes the ball?
questions.explain: Red tells the color of the ball. Color words are describing words.
questions.tip: Colors are describing words: red, blue, green.

questions.q: The sleepy cat yawned. Which word is the describing word?
questions.explain: Sleepy tells what the cat is like. Yawned is the action.
questions.tip: Adjectives answer the question: what kind? A sleepy cat.

questions.q: Which word describes a sound?
questions.explain: Loud tells what a sound is like.
questions.tip: Cover your ears: loud describes a big sound.

questions.q: Which word describes how something feels when you touch it?
questions.explain: Soft tells how something feels, like a pillow or a kitten.
questions.tip: Pet a kitten: soft!

questions.q: Which word describes how something looks?
questions.explain: Shiny tells how something looks, like a new coin.
questions.tip: Shiny things sparkle, and shiny describes them.

questions.q: Which word is NOT a describing word?
questions.say: Which word is not a describing word?
questions.explain: Truck names a thing, so it is a noun. Huge, sticky and bright describe things.
questions.tip: Does it name a person, place or thing? Then it is a noun, not a describing word.

questions.q: Which word fits? The ___ ice cream melted in the sun.
questions.say: Which word fits? The blank ice cream melted in the sun.
questions.explain: Cold describes the ice cream. Run, table and sing are not describing words.
questions.tip: Try each word: the cold ice cream. That sounds right!

questions.q: Which word comes first in ABC order: cow, egg, ant, fish?
questions.say: Which word comes first in A B C order? cow, egg, ant, fish.
questions.explain: Ant starts with a, and a comes first in the alphabet.
questions.tip: Sing the ABC song: the first letter you sing comes first.

questions.q: Which word comes first in ABC order: green, water, many, house?
questions.say: Which word comes first in A B C order? green, water, many, house.
questions.explain: G comes before h, m and w in the alphabet.
questions.tip: A, B, C, D, E, F, G: g comes along before h!

questions.q: Which word comes first in ABC order: bus, bed, bat, big?
questions.say: Which word comes first in A B C order? bus, bed, bat, big.
questions.explain: They all start with b, so look at the second letter: a comes before e, i and u.
questions.tip: Same first letter? Peek at the second letter!

questions.q: Which word comes first in ABC order: sun, star, snow, sock?
questions.say: Which word comes first in A B C order? sun, star, snow, sock.
questions.explain: They all start with s. The second letters are u, t, n and o, and n comes first.
questions.tip: Same first letter? Line up the second letters: n, o, t, u.

questions.q: Which word comes first in ABC order: cup, cat, cow, city?
questions.say: Which word comes first in A B C order? cup, cat, cow, city.
questions.explain: They all start with c. The second letters are u, a, o and i, and a comes first.
questions.tip: A is always first: cat beats city, cow and cup.

questions.q: Which word comes last in ABC order: moon, apple, zebra, yellow?
questions.say: Which word comes last in A B C order? moon, apple, zebra, yellow.
questions.explain: Z is the last letter of the alphabet, so zebra comes last.
questions.tip: X, Y and Z close the alphabet, and Z is the very end.

questions.q: Which letter comes right after M?
questions.explain: The alphabet goes L, M, N, O, P. N comes right after M.
questions.tip: L, M, N, O, P: say it fast, like one word: elemenopee!

questions.q: Put these words in ABC order: dog, ant, cat
questions.say: Put these words in A B C order: dog, ant, cat.
questions.explain: A comes first, then c, then d: ant, cat, dog.
questions.tip: A, B, C, D: ant, then cat, then dog.

questions.q: Which word comes first in ABC order: school, people, water, friend?
questions.say: Which word comes first in A B C order? school, people, water, friend.
questions.explain: F comes before p, s and w in the alphabet.
questions.tip: Friends come first!

questions.q: Which letter is missing? fr_end (a word for a pal)
questions.say: Which letter is missing from the word friend? f, r, blank, e, n, d.
questions.explain: Friend is spelled f-r-i-e-n-d.
questions.tip: A friend is there to the END: fri-END.

questions.q: Which letter is missing? sch_ol (where kids learn)
questions.say: Which letter is missing from the word school? s, c, h, blank, o, l.
questions.explain: School is spelled s-c-h-o-o-l, with two o's.
questions.tip: School has two o's, like two big eyes looking at the board.

questions.q: Which letter is missing? wat_r (you drink it)
questions.say: Which letter is missing from the word water? w, a, t, blank, r.
questions.explain: Water is spelled w-a-t-e-r.
questions.tip: Water ends in -er, just like river.

questions.q: Which letter is missing? pe_ple (men, women and kids)
questions.say: Which letter is missing from the word people? p, e, blank, p, l, e.
questions.explain: People is spelled p-e-o-p-l-e.
questions.tip: People has e and o side by side: p-E-O-ple.

questions.q: Which letter is missing? an_mal (a dog or a cat)
questions.say: Which letter is missing from the word animal? a, n, blank, m, a, l.
questions.explain: Animal is spelled a-n-i-m-a-l.
questions.tip: An-I-mal: I love animals!

questions.q: Which letter is missing? aga_n (one more time)
questions.say: Which letter is missing from the word again? a, g, a, blank, n.
questions.explain: Again is spelled a-g-a-i-n.
questions.tip: Again ends with the word gain: a-GAIN.

questions.q: Which letter is missing? _very (each one)
questions.say: Which letter is missing from the word every? blank, v, e, r, y.
questions.explain: Every is spelled e-v-e-r-y. It has the word very inside it.
questions.tip: Every is e plus very.

questions.q: Which letter is missing? wr_te (to put words on paper)
questions.say: Which letter is missing from the word write? w, r, blank, t, e.
questions.explain: Write is spelled w-r-i-t-e. It starts with a quiet w.
questions.tip: Write has a quiet w at the front and a quiet e at the end.

questions.q: sun + flower = ?
questions.say: Sun plus flower makes what word?
questions.explain: Sun and flower join to make sunflower, a tall yellow flower.
questions.tip: A compound word is two small words holding hands.

questions.q: rain + bow = ?
questions.say: Rain plus bow makes what word?
questions.explain: Rain and bow join to make rainbow.
questions.tip: After the rain, a bow of colors: rainbow!

questions.q: cup + cake = ?
questions.say: Cup plus cake makes what word?
questions.explain: Cup and cake join to make cupcake, a little cake.
questions.tip: A cupcake is a cake the size of a cup.

questions.q: foot + ball = ?
questions.say: Foot plus ball makes what word?
questions.explain: Foot and ball join to make football.
questions.tip: Kick the ball with your foot: football!

questions.q: snow + man = ?
questions.say: Snow plus man makes what word?
questions.explain: Snow and man join to make snowman.
questions.tip: A man made of snow is a snowman.

questions.q: star + fish = ?
questions.say: Star plus fish makes what word?
questions.explain: Star and fish join to make starfish, a sea animal shaped like a star.
questions.tip: A starfish looks like a star living in the sea.

questions.q: tooth + brush = ?
questions.say: Tooth plus brush makes what word?
questions.explain: Tooth and brush join to make toothbrush.
questions.tip: You brush your teeth with a toothbrush.

questions.q: butter + fly = ?
questions.say: Butter plus fly makes what word?
questions.explain: Butter and fly join to make butterfly.
questions.tip: A butterfly flutters by!

questions.q: Which word is a compound word?
questions.explain: Backpack is made of two words: back and pack.
questions.tip: Cut a compound word in two and you get two real words.

questions.q: Which two words make bedroom?
questions.explain: Bedroom is bed plus room: the room with your bed in it.
questions.tip: Find the two real words hiding inside.

questions.q: What is a syllable?
questions.explain: A syllable is one beat in a word. Ti-ger has two beats, so it has two syllables.
questions.tip: Clap the beats of your name: each clap is a syllable.

questions.q: How many syllables are in cat?
questions.say: How many syllables, or beats, are in the word cat?
questions.explain: Cat has one beat: cat.
questions.tip: Put your hand under your chin: your chin drops once for cat.

questions.q: How many syllables are in apple?
questions.say: How many syllables, or beats, are in the word apple?
questions.explain: Apple has two beats: ap-ple.
questions.tip: Clap it: ap-ple. Two claps!

questions.q: How many syllables are in tiger?
questions.say: How many syllables, or beats, are in the word tiger?
questions.explain: Tiger has two beats: ti-ger.
questions.tip: Roar it: ti-GER! Two beats.

questions.q: How many syllables are in rabbit?
questions.say: How many syllables, or beats, are in the word rabbit?
questions.explain: Rabbit has two beats: rab-bit.
questions.tip: Hop it out: rab-bit, two hops!

questions.q: How many syllables are in banana?
questions.say: How many syllables, or beats, are in the word banana?
questions.explain: Banana has three beats: ba-na-na.
questions.tip: Ba-na-na: three beats, like a monkey dance.

questions.q: How many syllables are in elephant?
questions.say: How many syllables, or beats, are in the word elephant?
questions.explain: Elephant has three beats: el-e-phant.
questions.tip: Stomp like an elephant: el-e-phant, three stomps!

questions.q: How many syllables are in dinosaur?
questions.say: How many syllables, or beats, are in the word dinosaur?
questions.explain: Dinosaur has three beats: di-no-saur.
questions.tip: Di-no-saur: three big dino steps.

questions.q: How many syllables are in butterfly?
questions.say: How many syllables, or beats, are in the word butterfly?
questions.explain: Butterfly has three beats: but-ter-fly.
questions.tip: Flap three times: but-ter-fly.

questions.q: How many syllables are in watermelon?
questions.say: How many syllables, or beats, are in the word watermelon?
questions.explain: Watermelon has four beats: wa-ter-mel-on.
questions.tip: Wa-ter-mel-on: four claps for a big fruit!

questions.q: What does unkind mean?
questions.explain: The prefix un- means not, so unkind means not kind.
questions.tip: Un- is like a big NO in front of a word.

questions.q: What does unsafe mean?
questions.explain: Un- means not, so unsafe means not safe.
questions.tip: Un- flips the word: safe becomes not safe.

questions.q: What does unlock mean?
questions.explain: Un- can mean to do the opposite. Unlock is the opposite of lock.
questions.tip: Lock the door, then unlock it to open it again.

questions.q: What does rewrite mean?
questions.explain: The prefix re- means again, so rewrite means write again.
questions.tip: Re- means do it again, like a replay.

questions.q: What does refill mean?
questions.explain: Re- means again, so refill means fill again.
questions.tip: Empty cup? Refill it: fill it again!

questions.q: Which word means read again?
questions.explain: Re- means again, so reread means read again.
questions.tip: Re- plus read: read it one more time.

questions.q: What does preheat mean?
questions.explain: The prefix pre- means before. You preheat the oven before you bake.
questions.tip: Pre- comes before, like a preview before a movie.

questions.q: What does joyful mean?
questions.explain: The suffix -ful means full of, so joyful means full of joy.
questions.tip: -ful means full: a cup full of joy!

questions.q: What does helpful mean?
questions.explain: -ful means full of, so a helpful person gives lots of help.
questions.tip: Helpful is full of help.

questions.q: What does fearless mean?
questions.explain: The suffix -less means without, so fearless means without fear.
questions.tip: -less means less and less, until there is none.

questions.q: What does useless mean?
questions.explain: -less means without, so useless means it has no use.
questions.tip: A pencil with no tip is useless: you can't use it.

questions.q: I ___ a good book last night.
questions.say: I blank a good book last night. Which word fits?
questions.explain: Read can sound like red when it happened in the past. Red is a color, and a reed is a tall grass.
questions.tip: You read a book; red is the color of a fire truck.

questions.q: The ___ shone in the sky.
questions.say: The blank shone in the sky. Which word fits?
questions.explain: The sun is the star in our sky. A son is a boy child.
questions.tip: The sUn is Up in the sky.

questions.q: I can ___ the music.
questions.say: I can blank the music. Which word fits?
questions.explain: Hear is what you do with your ears. Here means in this place.
questions.tip: You hEAR with your EAR!

questions.q: The wind ___ my hat off.
questions.say: The wind blank my hat off. Which word fits?
questions.explain: Blew is the past form of blow: the wind already pushed my hat. Blue is a color.
questions.tip: The wind blew; the sky is blue.

questions.q: Look at the big ships on the ___.
questions.say: Look at the big ships on the blank. Which word fits?
questions.explain: The sea is the ocean. See is what you do with your eyes.
questions.tip: You SEE with two E's, like two eyes.

questions.q: A ___ ran into the forest.
questions.say: A blank ran into the forest. Which word fits?
questions.explain: A deer is an animal. Dear is a kind word, like Dear Grandma.
questions.tip: Dear starts a letter; a deer runs in the forest.

questions.q: I have ___ hands.
questions.say: I have blank hands. Which word fits?
questions.explain: Two is the number 2.
questions.tip: Two, twins and twice all start with tw.

questions.q: Mom has one ___ and one daughter.
questions.say: Mom has one blank and one daughter. Which word fits?
questions.explain: A son is a boy child. The sun is in the sky.
questions.tip: The sun is Up high; a son is a boy.

questions.q: I ___ the answer!
questions.say: I blank the answer! Which word fits?
questions.explain: Know means to have it in your head. No is the opposite of yes.
questions.tip: Know has a quiet k: you KNOW it in your head.

questions.q: What did Max build?
questions.passage: Max wanted to build a house. First he chopped wood. Then he dug for stone. Last, he built the walls and put in a red door. Max was proud of his new house.
questions.explain: The story says Max wanted to build a house, and at the end he was proud of his new house.
questions.tip: The first sentence often tells what the story is about.

questions.q: What did Max do first?
questions.passage: Max wanted to build a house. First he chopped wood. Then he dug for stone. Last, he built the walls and put in a red door. Max was proud of his new house.
questions.explain: The story says: First he chopped wood. Then he dug for stone.
questions.tip: Look for the order words: first, then, last.

questions.q: How did Max feel at the end?
questions.passage: Max wanted to build a house. First he chopped wood. Then he dug for stone. Last, he built the walls and put in a red door. Max was proud of his new house.
questions.explain: The last sentence says Max was proud of his new house.
questions.tip: How a character feels at the end is often in the last sentence.

questions.q: Where did Lily find the kitten?
questions.passage: Lily heard a tiny cry from the bushes. She looked and found a gray kitten. It was cold and wet. Lily wrapped it in a towel and gave it warm milk. She named it Pebble.
questions.explain: Lily heard a cry from the bushes and found the kitten there.
questions.tip: Where questions ask about a place: look for words like in, on and at.

questions.q: Why did Lily wrap the kitten in a towel?
questions.passage: Lily heard a tiny cry from the bushes. She looked and found a gray kitten. It was cold and wet. Lily wrapped it in a towel and gave it warm milk. She named it Pebble.
questions.explain: The kitten was cold and wet, so the towel could dry it and keep it warm.
questions.tip: Why questions ask for a reason: look right before the action.

questions.q: What did Lily name the kitten?
questions.passage: Lily heard a tiny cry from the bushes. She looked and found a gray kitten. It was cold and wet. Lily wrapped it in a towel and gave it warm milk. She named it Pebble.
questions.explain: The last sentence says: She named it Pebble.
questions.tip: Look for the word named in the story.

questions.q: Why did Jo stop running?
questions.passage: Sam and Jo raced to the big oak tree. Jo was fast, but she tripped on a root. Sam stopped to help her up. Then they walked to the tree together and laughed.
questions.explain: The story says Jo was fast, but she tripped on a root.
questions.tip: The word but often tells you that something went wrong.

questions.q: What did Sam do when Jo fell?
questions.passage: Sam and Jo raced to the big oak tree. Jo was fast, but she tripped on a root. Sam stopped to help her up. Then they walked to the tree together and laughed.
questions.explain: Sam stopped racing to help Jo up.
questions.tip: Look back at the sentence right after Jo tripped.

questions.q: What does this story teach?
questions.passage: Sam and Jo raced to the big oak tree. Jo was fast, but she tripped on a root. Sam stopped to help her up. Then they walked to the tree together and laughed.
choices: Being kind matters more than winning
questions.explain: Sam gave up winning to help Jo, and they finished together, laughing.
questions.tip: The lesson is what the characters show us, not just what happens.

questions.q: What happened to Sam's tower?
questions.passage: Sam built a tall tower. A creeper sneaked up behind him. Boom! The tower was gone. Sam did not give up. He built it again, and this time he put a fence around it.
questions.explain: A creeper sneaked up, there was a boom, and the tower was gone.
questions.tip: Put the clues together: creeper plus boom means the tower blew up.

questions.q: What did Sam add the second time?
questions.passage: Sam built a tall tower. A creeper sneaked up behind him. Boom! The tower was gone. Sam did not give up. He built it again, and this time he put a fence around it.
questions.explain: The last sentence says he put a fence around the tower.
questions.tip: The second time comes later in the story, so look near the end.

questions.q: Which word best describes Sam?
questions.passage: Sam built a tall tower. A creeper sneaked up behind him. Boom! The tower was gone. Sam did not give up. He built it again, and this time he put a fence around it.
questions.explain: Sam did not give up and built his tower again. Someone who keeps trying is determined.
questions.tip: Determined means you keep going even when it is hard.

questions.q: Where did Mia's friends hide?
questions.passage: Mia's friends hid behind the couch. When Mia opened the door, they jumped out and yelled, "Surprise!" Mia laughed so hard she dropped her backpack. Then everyone ate cake.
questions.explain: The first sentence says the friends hid behind the couch.
questions.tip: Where questions are answered by a place.

questions.q: Why did Mia drop her backpack?
questions.passage: Mia's friends hid behind the couch. When Mia opened the door, they jumped out and yelled, "Surprise!" Mia laughed so hard she dropped her backpack. Then everyone ate cake.
questions.explain: The story says Mia laughed so hard she dropped her backpack.
questions.tip: The word so often comes before what happened because of it.

questions.q: What happened last?
questions.passage: Mia's friends hid behind the couch. When Mia opened the door, they jumped out and yelled, "Surprise!" Mia laughed so hard she dropped her backpack. Then everyone ate cake.
questions.explain: The story ends with: Then everyone ate cake.
questions.tip: What happened last is usually in the last sentence.

questions.q: How many times did Kai fall into the lava?
questions.passage: Kai played a very hard obby. He fell into the lava ten times. His sister said, "Take your time and look before you jump." Kai tried it. He reached the flag at last!
questions.explain: The story says he fell into the lava ten times.
questions.tip: Number questions: look for a number word in the story.

questions.q: Who gave Kai advice?
questions.passage: Kai played a very hard obby. He fell into the lava ten times. His sister said, "Take your time and look before you jump." Kai tried it. He reached the flag at last!
questions.explain: His sister told him to take his time.
questions.tip: Who questions are answered by a person.

questions.q: What advice did Kai get?
questions.passage: Kai played a very hard obby. He fell into the lava ten times. His sister said, "Take your time and look before you jump." Kai tried it. He reached the flag at last!
choices: Take your time and look before you jump
questions.explain: His sister said: Take your time and look before you jump. It worked!
questions.tip: Advice is a helpful idea someone gives you.

questions.q: What did Ben have at the start?
questions.passage: Ben had two apples. Zoe had two cookies. Ben liked cookies, and Zoe liked apples. They traded one apple for one cookie. Now both of them had a snack they liked.
questions.explain: The first sentence says Ben had two apples.
questions.tip: At the start means look at the beginning of the story.

questions.q: What did Ben and Zoe trade?
questions.passage: Ben had two apples. Zoe had two cookies. Ben liked cookies, and Zoe liked apples. They traded one apple for one cookie. Now both of them had a snack they liked.
questions.explain: They traded one apple for one cookie.
questions.tip: A trade is a swap: I give you one, you give me one.

questions.q: How did Ben and Zoe most likely feel at the end?
questions.passage: Ben had two apples. Zoe had two cookies. Ben liked cookies, and Zoe liked apples. They traded one apple for one cookie. Now both of them had a snack they liked.
questions.explain: Both of them had a snack they liked, so they were most likely happy.
questions.tip: Think how you would feel if you got a snack you like.

questions.q: Why was school closed?
questions.passage: It snowed all night. In the morning, school was closed. Leo and his dad built a snow fort. Then they drank hot cocoa by the fire. It was the best day of winter.
questions.explain: It snowed all night, so in the morning school was closed for a snow day.
questions.tip: The cause often comes first, and what happens because of it comes next.

questions.q: What did Leo and his dad build?
questions.passage: It snowed all night. In the morning, school was closed. Leo and his dad built a snow fort. Then they drank hot cocoa by the fire. It was the best day of winter.
questions.explain: The story says Leo and his dad built a snow fort.
questions.tip: Look for the word built in the story.

questions.q: What did they do after they built the fort?
questions.passage: It snowed all night. In the morning, school was closed. Leo and his dad built a snow fort. Then they drank hot cocoa by the fire. It was the best day of winter.
questions.explain: Then they drank hot cocoa by the fire.
questions.tip: After means next: look for the word then.

questions.q: What do bees collect from flowers?
questions.passage: Honeybees are busy insects. They fly from flower to flower to collect nectar. Back at the hive, they turn the nectar into honey. Bees also help plants grow by spreading pollen.
questions.explain: Bees fly from flower to flower to collect nectar, a sweet juice.
questions.tip: Nectar is the flower's sweet drink.

questions.q: What do honeybees make from nectar?
questions.passage: Honeybees are busy insects. They fly from flower to flower to collect nectar. Back at the hive, they turn the nectar into honey. Bees also help plants grow by spreading pollen.
questions.explain: Back at the hive, bees turn the nectar into honey.
questions.tip: Nectar in, honey out!

questions.q: What is this passage mostly about?
questions.passage: Honeybees are busy insects. They fly from flower to flower to collect nectar. Back at the hive, they turn the nectar into honey. Bees also help plants grow by spreading pollen.
choices: How bees are busy and helpful
questions.explain: Every sentence tells something busy or helpful that bees do.
questions.tip: The main idea is what most of the sentences are about.

questions.q: What warms the water in lakes and oceans?
questions.passage: The sun warms the water in lakes and oceans. The water rises into the air as vapor. High up, it cools and forms clouds. When the drops get heavy, they fall as rain.
questions.explain: The first sentence says the sun warms the water.
questions.tip: The sun is Earth's big heater.

questions.q: What forms when the water cools high up?
questions.passage: The sun warms the water in lakes and oceans. The water rises into the air as vapor. High up, it cools and forms clouds. When the drops get heavy, they fall as rain.
questions.explain: High up, the water cools and forms clouds.
questions.tip: Up, up, up the water goes, and clouds are what it makes.

questions.q: When does the rain fall?
questions.passage: The sun warms the water in lakes and oceans. The water rises into the air as vapor. High up, it cools and forms clouds. When the drops get heavy, they fall as rain.
questions.explain: When the drops in the clouds get heavy, they fall as rain.
questions.tip: Heavy drops can't float, so down they come!

questions.q: What do penguins use their wings for?
questions.passage: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. They use their wings to swim very fast. Many penguins live where it is very cold. A thick layer of fat keeps them warm.
questions.explain: Penguins use their wings to swim very fast.
questions.tip: A penguin's wings work like flippers.

questions.q: What keeps penguins warm?
questions.passage: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. They use their wings to swim very fast. Many penguins live where it is very cold. A thick layer of fat keeps them warm.
questions.explain: The last sentence says a thick layer of fat keeps them warm.
questions.tip: Fat under the skin is like a warm coat inside the body.

questions.q: Can penguins fly?
questions.passage: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. They use their wings to swim very fast. Many penguins live where it is very cold. A thick layer of fat keeps them warm.
questions.explain: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. They swim instead.
questions.tip: Penguins fly through the water, not the air!

questions.q: What does a seed need to start growing?
questions.passage: A seed needs water, air, and warmth to start growing. First, a root grows down. Next, a stem pushes up. Then leaves open in the sunlight, and the plant can make its own food.
questions.explain: The first sentence says a seed needs water, air, and warmth to start growing.
questions.tip: A seed wakes up with a drink, a breath, and a warm blanket of soil.

questions.q: What grows first?
questions.passage: A seed needs water, air, and warmth to start growing. First, a root grows down. Next, a stem pushes up. Then leaves open in the sunlight, and the plant can make its own food.
questions.explain: First, a root grows down. Next comes the stem.
questions.tip: Roots first, like the anchor of a boat.

questions.q: What can the plant do after its leaves open?
questions.passage: A seed needs water, air, and warmth to start growing. First, a root grows down. Next, a stem pushes up. Then leaves open in the sunlight, and the plant can make its own food.
questions.explain: Leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant.
questions.tip: Leaves are the plant's kitchen.

questions.q: When do most owls hunt?
questions.passage: Most owls hunt at night. Their big eyes help them see in the dark. Owls can turn their heads almost all the way around. They fly almost without a sound, so mice do not hear them coming.
questions.explain: The first sentence says most owls hunt at night.
questions.tip: Night hunters hunt at night!

questions.q: Why don't mice hear the owls coming?
questions.passage: Most owls hunt at night. Their big eyes help them see in the dark. Owls can turn their heads almost all the way around. They fly almost without a sound, so mice do not hear them coming.
choices: Owls fly almost without a sound
questions.explain: Owls fly almost without a sound, so mice do not hear them.
questions.tip: The word so connects a reason to what happens.

questions.q: What helps owls see in the dark?
questions.passage: Most owls hunt at night. Their big eyes help them see in the dark. Owls can turn their heads almost all the way around. They fly almost without a sound, so mice do not hear them coming.
questions.explain: Their big eyes help them see in the dark.
questions.tip: Big eyes catch more light, like big windows.

questions.q: Why do dolphins come up to the top of the water?
questions.passage: Dolphins live in the ocean, but they are not fish. They are mammals, so they breathe air. Dolphins come up to the top of the water to breathe. They talk to each other with clicks and whistles.
questions.explain: Dolphins are mammals that breathe air, so they come up to breathe.
questions.tip: Dolphins breathe through a blowhole on top of their heads.

questions.q: What kind of animal is a dolphin?
questions.passage: Dolphins live in the ocean, but they are not fish. They are mammals, so they breathe air. Dolphins come up to the top of the water to breathe. They talk to each other with clicks and whistles.
questions.explain: The passage says dolphins are not fish. They are mammals.
questions.tip: Mammals breathe air and feed their babies milk, just like people.

questions.q: How do dolphins talk to each other?
questions.passage: Dolphins live in the ocean, but they are not fish. They are mammals, so they breathe air. Dolphins come up to the top of the water to breathe. They talk to each other with clicks and whistles.
questions.explain: The last sentence says they talk with clicks and whistles.
questions.tip: Click, click, wheee: dolphin talk!

questions.q: In 'The fluffy cat slept,' which word is an adjective?
questions.explain: Fluffy describes the noun cat, so it is an adjective.
questions.tip: Adjectives Add details to nouns: fluffy, red, tiny.

questions.q: In 'She ran quickly,' which word is an adverb?
questions.explain: Quickly tells how she ran, so it is an adverb.
questions.tip: Many adverbs end in -ly, and they ADD to the verb.

questions.q: In 'The ball is under the bed,' what part of speech is 'under'?
questions.explain: Under shows the relationship between the ball and the bed, so it is a preposition.
questions.tip: A preposition is anywhere a cat can go with a box: in, on, under, by.

questions.q: What part of speech is 'and'?
questions.explain: And joins words or groups of words, so it is a conjunction.
questions.tip: Conjunction junction: and, but, and or hook words together like train cars.

questions.q: Which word is a pronoun?
questions.explain: They takes the place of a noun, so it is a pronoun.
questions.tip: Pronouns are PROs at replacing nouns: he, she, it, they.

questions.q: A word that describes a noun is called a(n)...
questions.explain: Adjectives describe nouns, like red, tall, or happy.
questions.tip: Adjectives describe nouns: a red ball, a big dog.

questions.q: A word that tells how, when, or where an action happens is a(n)...
questions.explain: Adverbs describe verbs, like slowly, yesterday, or here.
questions.tip: Adverbs answer how, when, and where: quickly, today, here.

questions.q: Which word is a proper noun?
questions.explain: Texas names a specific place, so it is a proper noun and starts with a capital letter.
questions.tip: Proper nouns are proper names, so they wear a capital letter.

questions.q: In 'Wow, that is amazing!' what part of speech is 'Wow'?
questions.explain: An interjection is a word that shows sudden feeling, like wow or oops.
questions.tip: Interjections Interrupt with feeling: Wow! Oops! Hooray!

questions.q: In 'The children laughed loudly,' which word is the verb?
questions.explain: Laughed is the action the children did.
questions.tip: Find the verb by asking: what did they do?

questions.q: What is the plural of 'child'?
questions.explain: Child has an irregular plural: children.
questions.tip: One child, two children, a whole playground of children.

questions.q: What is the plural of 'mouse' (the animal)?
questions.explain: Mouse has an irregular plural: mice.
questions.tip: One mouse, two mice: the mice think cheese is nice.

questions.q: What is the plural of 'box'?
questions.explain: Words ending in x, s, sh, ch, or z usually add -es.
questions.tip: If adding just s sounds like a hiss you can't say (boxs), add -es.

questions.q: What is the plural of 'baby'?
questions.explain: When a word ends in a consonant plus y, change the y to i and add -es.
questions.tip: Consonant plus y? Y flies away and -ies takes its place: babies.

questions.q: What is the plural of 'day'?
questions.explain: When a word ends in a vowel plus y, just add -s.
questions.tip: Vowel plus y? Y stays: days, toys, keys.

questions.q: What is the plural of 'leaf'?
questions.explain: Many words ending in f change the f to v and add -es: leaf, leaves.
questions.tip: In fall the leaves fall, and the f turns into v.

questions.q: What is the plural of 'tooth'?
questions.explain: Tooth has an irregular plural: teeth.
questions.tip: One tooth, two teeth: just like one goose, two geese.

questions.q: What is the plural of 'sheep'?
questions.explain: Sheep stays the same for one or many.
questions.tip: Sheep, deer, and fish: count a flock of them and they still sound the same.

questions.q: What is the plural of 'tomato'?
questions.explain: Tomato adds -es: tomatoes. Potato works the same way.
questions.tip: Tomatoes and potatoes both have toes!

questions.q: What is the plural of 'foot'?
questions.explain: Foot has an irregular plural: feet.
questions.tip: One foot, two feet: oo turns to ee, like tooth and teeth.

questions.q: ___ going to the park after school.
questions.explain: They're is short for they are: They are going to the park.
questions.tip: They're has an apostrophe because a letter is missing: they are.

questions.q: The book is over ___.
questions.explain: There tells about a place.
questions.tip: There has 'here' inside it, so it points to a place.

questions.q: The kids rode ___ bikes.
questions.explain: Their shows that something belongs to them.
questions.tip: Their has 'heir' inside, and an heir owns things.

questions.q: She has ___ cats.
questions.explain: Two is the number 2.
questions.tip: Two has a w, like twin and twice: words that are all about two.

questions.q: This soup is ___ hot to eat.
questions.explain: Too means more than enough, or also.
questions.tip: Too has an extra o, so it means extra or also.

questions.q: The dog wagged ___ tail.
questions.explain: Its shows ownership. It's always means it is or it has.
questions.tip: Its, his, hers: possessive pronouns never use an apostrophe.

questions.q: ___ raining outside.
questions.explain: It's is short for it is: It is raining outside.
questions.tip: Try 'it is': if it fits, use it's.

questions.q: Did you ___ the thunder?
questions.explain: Hear is what you do with your ear. Here means this place.
questions.tip: You hear with your ear, and 'hear' has 'ear' inside.

questions.q: ___ ready for the trip?
questions.explain: You're is short for you are: Are you ready? You are ready.
questions.tip: Try 'you are': you are ready, so you're ready.

questions.q: ___ backpack is this?
questions.explain: Whose asks who owns something. Who's means who is or who has.
questions.tip: Who's means who is; whose asks who owns it.

questions.q: Synonyms are words that...
choices: mean the same or nearly the same
sound the same but are spelled differently
questions.explain: Synonyms have similar meanings, like big and large. Antonyms are opposites.
questions.tip: Synonym and Same both start with S; Antonym and Anti (against) both start with A.

questions.q: Which word is a synonym for 'happy'?
questions.explain: Glad means about the same as happy.
questions.tip: Happy and glad both make you smile.

questions.q: Which word is an antonym for 'brave'?
questions.explain: Cowardly is the opposite of brave. Bold and heroic are synonyms.
questions.tip: Antonym starts like 'anti', which means against: opposites.

questions.q: Which word is a synonym for 'big'?
questions.explain: Large means about the same as big.
questions.tip: Big and large both fill up the room.

questions.q: Which word is an antonym for 'ancient'?
questions.explain: Ancient means very old. Modern means new or recent.
questions.tip: Ancient dinosaurs, modern cars.

questions.q: Which word is a synonym for 'quick'?
questions.explain: Fast and quick mean nearly the same thing.
questions.tip: Quick and fast both win the race.

questions.q: Which word is an antonym for 'generous'?
questions.explain: A generous person shares. A selfish person does not.
questions.tip: Generous gives, selfish keeps.

questions.q: Which word is a synonym for 'begin'?
questions.explain: Begin and start mean the same thing.
questions.tip: Begin and start are both how you start!

questions.q: Which word is an antonym for 'difficult'?
questions.explain: Easy is the opposite of difficult. Hard, tough, and tricky are synonyms.
questions.tip: Easy as pie is the opposite of difficult.

questions.q: Which word is a synonym for 'tiny'?
questions.explain: Tiny means very small.
questions.tip: A tiny ant is very small.

questions.q: What does the prefix 'un-' mean in 'unhappy'?
questions.explain: Unhappy means not happy.
questions.tip: Un- undoes things: unhappy, untie, unlock.

questions.q: What does the prefix 're-' mean in 'redo'?
questions.explain: Redo means to do again.
questions.tip: Re- is like replay: do it again!

questions.q: What does the prefix 'pre-' mean in 'preview'?
questions.explain: A preview is a look at something before it happens.
questions.tip: Pre- comes before, like preschool comes before kindergarten.

questions.q: What does the suffix '-less' mean in 'careless'?
questions.explain: Careless means without care.
questions.tip: Careless means you care less: without care.

questions.q: What does the suffix '-ful' mean in 'hopeful'?
questions.explain: Hopeful means full of hope.
questions.tip: Hopeful is full of hope, but the suffix -ful keeps only one l.

questions.q: What does the suffix '-er' mean in 'teacher'?
questions.explain: A teacher is one who teaches.
questions.tip: Teacher, baker, painter: -er is the one who does it.

questions.q: What does the prefix 'dis-' mean in 'disagree'?
questions.explain: Disagree means to not agree.
questions.tip: Dis- dismisses things: disagree, dislike, disappear.

questions.q: What does 'misspell' mean?
questions.explain: The prefix mis- means wrongly or badly. Note the two s's: mis + spell.
questions.tip: Mis- is like mistake, so misspell means spelling by mistake.

questions.q: Which word has a prefix?
questions.explain: Unlock has the prefix un- at the start. Locker and locked have suffixes at the end.
questions.tip: A prefix comes first, because pre means before.

questions.q: Which suffix turns 'slow' into an adverb?
questions.explain: Adding -ly makes slowly, which tells how something is done.
questions.tip: Add -ly to tell how: slowly, quietly, happily.

questions.q: Which sentence uses commas correctly in a list?
choices: I bought apples, bananas, and grapes.
I bought, apples bananas and grapes.
I bought apples bananas, and, grapes.
questions.explain: Commas separate the items in a list of three or more.
questions.tip: Commas are little breaths between items, like reading a grocery list aloud.

questions.q: Which is the correct contraction for 'do not'?
questions.explain: The apostrophe goes where the letter o was removed: don't.
questions.tip: The apostrophe sits where the o went missing: do not, don't.

questions.q: Which is the correct contraction for 'I will'?
questions.explain: The apostrophe replaces the missing letters wi: I'll.
questions.tip: An apostrophe is a patch where letters fell out: I wi-ll becomes I'll.

questions.q: Which sentence uses quotation marks correctly?
questions.explain: Put a comma before the quote, and in American English the period goes inside the closing quotation mark.
questions.tip: In America, periods and commas tuck inside the quotation marks like kids in bed.

questions.q: How do you show that a bike belongs to Sam?
questions.explain: Add an apostrophe and s to a singular name to show ownership.
questions.tip: Apostrophe-s means it belongs to someone: Sam's bike.

questions.q: How do you write the toys that belong to several dogs?
questions.explain: For a plural noun ending in s, add just an apostrophe after the s.
questions.tip: Many dogs? The s comes first, then the apostrophe hugs it from behind.

questions.q: Which date is punctuated correctly?
questions.explain: Put a comma between the day and the year.
questions.tip: A comma keeps the day and year from bumping into each other.

questions.q: Which is the correct greeting for a friendly letter?
questions.explain: A friendly letter greeting ends with a comma.
questions.tip: A friendly letter waves hello with a comma.

questions.q: Which sentence uses a comma correctly?
choices: Yes, I would like some juice.
Yes I, would like some juice.
Yes I would, like some juice.
questions.explain: Put a comma after an introductory word like yes, no, or well.
questions.tip: Yes, no, and well take a little comma breath.

questions.q: What does an exclamation point show?
questions.explain: An exclamation point ends a sentence with strong feeling, like 'We won!'
questions.tip: An exclamation point is a sentence jumping with excitement!

questions.q: What does 'enormous' mean?
questions.explain: Enormous means huge or very large.
questions.tip: Enormous is a big word for something big.

questions.q: What does 'fragile' mean?
questions.explain: Fragile things, like glass, break easily.
questions.tip: Boxes with glass inside are stamped FRAGILE: handle with care!

questions.q: What does 'cautious' mean?
questions.explain: A cautious person is careful to avoid danger or mistakes.
questions.tip: Cautious sounds like caution, like a yellow caution sign.

questions.q: 'The weary hikers rested after the long climb.' What does 'weary' mean?
questions.explain: The clues 'rested' and 'long climb' show that weary means tired.
questions.tip: Weary hikers are worn out: weary and worn both start with w.

questions.q: 'The arid desert had not seen rain in months.' What does 'arid' mean?
questions.explain: No rain for months is the clue: arid means very dry.
questions.tip: Arid: A Really Incredibly Dry place.

questions.q: What does 'predict' mean?
questions.explain: When you predict, you make a smart guess about what will happen next.
questions.tip: Pre means before and dict means say: predict means to say it before it happens.

questions.q: Words around an unknown word that help you figure out its meaning are called...
questions.explain: Context clues are hints in the nearby words and sentences.
questions.tip: Context clues are detective clues hiding in nearby words.

questions.q: The main idea of a passage is...
questions.explain: The main idea is the most important point the passage is about.
questions.tip: The main idea is the umbrella; the details are the raindrops under it.

questions.q: What does 'reluctant' mean?
questions.explain: A reluctant person does not want to do something.
questions.tip: Reluctant is how you feel being dragged to clean your room.

questions.q: If an author's purpose is to persuade, the author wants to...
questions.explain: Persuade means to convince someone to believe or do something.
questions.tip: Persuasive ads want you to buy something: they persuade.

questions.q: Each of the students ___ a book.
questions.explain: The subject is 'each', which is singular, so it takes 'has'.
questions.tip: Each, every, and everyone are singular: each one has.

questions.q: The dogs in the yard ___ barking.
questions.explain: The subject is 'dogs', which is plural. 'In the yard' does not change it.
questions.tip: Cross out the prepositional phrase, then match the verb: the dogs are.

questions.q: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready.
questions.explain: With neither/nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'students', which is plural.
questions.tip: Neither/nor: the closest subject is the boss of the verb.

questions.q: Either my brothers or my sister ___ coming.
questions.explain: With either/or, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'sister', which is singular.
questions.tip: Closest subject wins: my sister is.

questions.q: The box of crayons ___ on the shelf.
questions.explain: The subject is 'box', not 'crayons', so the verb is singular.
questions.tip: Cross out 'of crayons': the box is.

questions.q: Everyone ___ invited to the party.
questions.explain: Everyone is a singular indefinite pronoun.
questions.tip: Every ONE is one, so everyone is.

questions.q: Mathematics ___ my favorite subject.
questions.explain: Mathematics ends in s but names one subject, so it takes a singular verb.
questions.tip: Math is one subject even with an s, just like the news is.

questions.q: Tom and Maria ___ on the team.
questions.explain: Two subjects joined by 'and' make a plural subject.
questions.tip: And adds up: Tom plus Maria equals they, and they are.

questions.q: There ___ three apples on the table.
questions.explain: In a 'there' sentence, the subject comes after the verb. Here it is 'apples', which is plural.
questions.tip: Flip it around: three apples are there.

questions.q: One of my friends ___ a cat.
questions.explain: The subject is 'one', which is singular. 'Of my friends' is a prepositional phrase.
questions.tip: Spot the ONE: one of my friends has.

questions.q: Sam and ___ went to the store.
questions.explain: Use the subject pronoun 'I'. Test it alone: 'I went to the store.'
questions.tip: Drop the other person: you'd say 'I went,' not 'me went'.

questions.q: The coach gave the ball to Jake and ___.
questions.explain: After a preposition like 'to', use the object pronoun 'me'. Test: 'gave the ball to me.'
questions.tip: Drop Jake: 'gave the ball to me'.

questions.q: Between you and ___, this test is easy.
questions.explain: 'Between' is a preposition, so it takes the object pronoun 'me'.
questions.tip: Between you and me: prepositions take 'me'.

questions.q: Which word is a possessive pronoun?
questions.explain: Theirs shows ownership: The house is theirs.
questions.tip: Theirs, ours, yours, his, hers: possessive pronouns never need an apostrophe.

questions.q: Which pronoun is reflexive?
questions.explain: Reflexive pronouns end in -self or -selves and refer back to the subject.
questions.tip: Reflexive pronouns reflect back like a mirror: himself, herself.

questions.q: Which pronoun is in the objective case?
questions.explain: Us is used as an object: They invited us.
questions.tip: Objects get acted on: they invited us, just like the ball gets kicked.

questions.q: 'Maria lost her phone, but she found it later.' What does 'it' refer to?
questions.explain: The antecedent of 'it' is the noun it replaces: the phone.
questions.tip: Look back for the noun that makes sense in its place.

questions.q: ___ is going to the game tonight?
questions.explain: Who is the subject of 'is going', so use 'who'.
questions.tip: Answer with he: 'He is going,' so use who.

questions.q: A pronoun takes the place of a...
questions.explain: Pronouns like he, she, and it replace nouns.
questions.tip: A pronoun works FOR a noun, like a substitute teacher.

questions.q: Which sentence uses pronouns correctly?
questions.explain: The subject of a sentence needs subject pronouns: she and I.
questions.tip: Test each alone: she studied, I studied.

questions.q: An independent clause...
choices: can stand alone as a sentence
questions.explain: An independent clause has a subject and a verb and expresses a complete thought.
questions.tip: Independent clauses are independent: they stand on their own two feet.

questions.q: Which is a dependent clause?
questions.explain: 'Because it was raining' has a subject and verb but cannot stand alone.
questions.tip: A dependent clause depends on a buddy, like a little kid holding a hand.

questions.q: 'I wanted to play, but it was raining.' What type of sentence is this?
questions.explain: Two independent clauses joined by 'but' make a compound sentence.
questions.tip: Compound means combined: two complete sentences joined with a FANBOYS word.

questions.q: 'Although I was tired, I finished my homework.' What type of sentence is this?
questions.explain: One dependent clause plus one independent clause makes a complex sentence.
questions.tip: Complex sentences have a helper clause, often starting with 'although' or 'because'.

questions.q: Which is a sentence fragment?
choices: The dog ran down the street.
questions.explain: 'Running down the street' has no subject or main verb. 'Run!' is a command with an understood subject, you.
questions.tip: No subject or no main verb? It is just a fragment, a broken piece.

questions.q: Which is a run-on sentence?
choices: I like pizza I eat it every day.
I like pizza, and I eat it every day.
I like pizza; I eat it every day.
questions.explain: Two independent clauses with no punctuation or conjunction between them form a run-on.
questions.tip: Run-ons run right through the stop sign.

questions.q: Which word is a subordinating conjunction?
questions.explain: 'Because' begins a dependent clause. And, but, and or are coordinating conjunctions.
questions.tip: AAAWWUBBIS: after, although, as, when, while, until, because, before, if, since.

questions.q: FANBOYS lists the coordinating conjunctions. Which word is one of them?
questions.explain: FANBOYS: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so.
questions.tip: FANBOYS: For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So.

questions.q: What is the complete subject of 'The tall girl with red hair won the race'?
choices: The tall girl with red hair
questions.explain: The complete subject is who or what the sentence is about, with all its describing words.
questions.tip: Ask who or what did it: the whole group of words is the complete subject.

questions.q: Which correctly joins two independent clauses?
choices: I studied hard; I passed the test.
I studied hard, I passed the test.
I studied hard I passed the test.
questions.explain: A semicolon can join two closely related independent clauses. A comma alone creates a comma splice.
questions.tip: A semicolon is a period stacked on a comma: strong enough to join two full sentences.

questions.q: 'Her smile was as bright as the sun' is an example of...
questions.explain: A simile compares two things using 'like' or 'as'.
questions.tip: SImile is SImilar: it compares using like or as.

questions.q: 'The classroom was a zoo' is an example of...
questions.explain: A metaphor says one thing is another, without 'like' or 'as'.
questions.tip: A metaphor just says it IS the thing.

questions.q: 'The wind whispered through the trees' is an example of...
questions.explain: Personification gives human actions, like whispering, to non-human things.
questions.tip: Personification gives a thing a PERSONality.

questions.q: 'I've told you a million times!' is an example of...
questions.explain: Hyperbole is extreme exaggeration for effect.
questions.tip: Hyperbole is hyper: super-duper exaggerated.

questions.q: Words like 'buzz,' 'sizzle,' and 'pop' are examples of...
questions.explain: Onomatopoeia is a word that imitates the sound it names.
questions.tip: Onomatopoeia: Boom! Pow! Splash! The word sounds like itself.

questions.q: 'Sally sells seashells by the seashore' is an example of...
questions.explain: Alliteration repeats the same beginning consonant sound in nearby words.
questions.tip: Alliteration: lots of letters lining up.

questions.q: 'It's raining cats and dogs' is an example of...
questions.explain: An idiom is a phrase whose meaning differs from its literal words. This one means it is raining hard.
questions.tip: Picture an idiom literally: cats and dogs falling from the sky!

questions.q: What is the difference between a simile and a metaphor?
